items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: There was a guy called Berrian Shute, and he was very good. ... I learned chord changes, I learned harmony, I learned basic Western harmony from this course.

ctx.x: How about the music professors? © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

Well I took the music appreciation course. There was a guy called Berrian Shute, and he was very good. It was a very good course and I learned chord changes, I learned harmony, I learned basic Western harmony from this course. And that was how I began to get my changes together and I realized hey, there’s a whole scheme here that you could know. And so I — but they had no interest in jazz whatever. None. This was an odd little hobby like who knows what, collecting pottery or something or other that some of the…
I don’t know if you would have ever had this conversation with your bandmates or your listening mates, but do you recall if you thought of this music at the time as an art form?
